test_title: RRB Technician Grade III Official Paper (Held On: 23 Dec, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Which of the following is INCORRECT about parenchyma?

options.text: It consists of relatively unspecialised cells with thin cell walls.
In aquatic plants, large air cavities are present in parenchyma to help them float.
It allows the bending of various parts of a plant like tendrils and stems of climbers without breaking.
The cells of parenchyma are living cells and are usually loosely arranged.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Parenchyma cells are known for their thin cell walls and relatively unspecialized functions.
 
• In aquatic plants, parenchyma cells contain large air cavities that aid in buoyancy, helping the plants float.
 
• Parenchyma cells are living cells and are usually loosely arranged, which allows for the storage of nutrients and water.
 
• Unlike collenchyma cells, parenchyma does not provide flexibility and strength to plant parts like tendrils and stems of climbers; this is a function of collenchyma cells.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Collenchyma Cells**

 
 
• Collenchyma cells have thicker cell walls compared to parenchyma and are typically found in regions of the plant that require support.
 
• These cells provide structural support and flexibility to the plant, allowing it to withstand various mechanical stresses.
 
 
 
• **Sclerenchyma Cells**
 
 
• Sclerenchyma cells are known for their extremely thick cell walls and are usually dead at maturity.
 
• These cells provide the primary structural support in plants, contributing to the hardness of seeds and nuts.
 
 
 
• **Functions of Parenchyma Cells**
 
 
• They are involved in storage, secretion, and photosynthesis in plants.
 
• Parenchyma cells also play a crucial role in the healing and repair of plant tissues.
 
 
 
• **Types of Parenchyma**
 
 
• **Chlorenchyma:** Contains chloroplasts and is involved in photosynthesis.
 
• **Aerenchyma:** Contains large air spaces to facilitate buoyancy in aquatic plants.
